newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: TOO EARLY TO CONSIDER GST PRIME MINISTER
The Prime Minister says it's far too early to say whether the Federal Government would consider introducting a GST if it wins a second term of office.
John Howard has told ABC radio that he's keeping his promise that there won't be a goods and services tax during this parliamentary term.
This follows calls by the West Australian Premier Richard Court for a GST to be put back on the political agenda.
The Prime Minister says he won't be considering the matter until at least the end of the current term.
BID FOR NEW WOOL GROUP LAUNCHED
Angry woolgrowers dissatisfied over the performance of current grower bodies have launched a bid for one new national organisation.
Growers from from six states have formed a steering committee to launch the Australian Woolgrowers Association.
Chairman Peter Laird says current groups aren't giving producers a vote and it's time for those growers to regain management of their industry.
CHILDREN KILLED WITH KITCHEN KNIFE
Police say two children, found dead in their Deer Park house last night, were killed with a kitchen knife by their step father.
The 24 year-old man then killed himself by lying in the path of a truck on the Western Ring Road at Ardeer.
Autopsies will be conducted on the three bodies this morning and the coroner has been briefed by police.
Police say a mother of four left her children in the care of her 24 year-old husband to play bingo with relatives.
She returned to her Wakool Avenue house just after ten last night and found the bodies of her 9 year-old daughter and 7 year-old son. Both had their throats cut.
PROTEST OVER LOSS OF ITALIAN LANGUAGE COURSE
The Italian community in Tasmania has made a strong protest to the University of Tasmania over its abolition of the Italian language course next year.
Twenty community groups including the Italian Cultural Council of Tasmania and the Australian Italian Club have joined forces to convey, what they say, is resentment and insult at the loss.
The cut is one of several the University says its been forced to make following the Federal Government's decision to cut its budget by A$10 million.

The Italian Government had offered to pay costs for one of the two lecturers needed to run the course, however, the university's decision remains unchanged. The groups say the knock-back appears unfriendly and offensive.
NEW NAME FOR SA'S MFP
South Australia's much-maligned multi-function polis, or at least its central development project, gets a new name today.
In a further effort to improve the M-F-P's image, the name will be applied to the urban development, the so-called smart city to be built in Adelaide's north.
It'll be named after a deceased South Australian hero.
The Premier, John Olsen, will reveal who this morning, at a ceremony at the South Australian Museum.
The umbrella organisation will keep the name, M-F-P Development Corporation.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
